title: red-pipeline reads a real red job older than 10 unstarted main pipelines as green, since the idle stop returns the newest finished pipeline
goal: latest_pipeline (bl_intake.py), when its read stops after IDLE_PIPELINES pipelines in a row in which no job ran, returns "not checked" (None with a note naming the stop) and never a green verdict for the newest finished pipeline, so a red job that ran behind more than ten unstarted pipelines is not reported green by red-pipeline --status or the intake ci detector; a test in test_intake.py plants 100 GitLab pipelines with the red job at the fifteenth and sees the note, and a red job at the fifth is still found; the docs sentences about the window (backlog.md, tools.md, the docstring) say the answer is "not checked". Found by the SP-mguj7foz review (BG-h4wygoak).
repro_reason: the repro stubs the forge CLI calls to plant 100 main pipelines whose jobs are all manual but one red job at the fifteenth, and exits 1 while latest_pipeline answers a green verdict
